title: Shopify QuickBooks Integration Not Syncing? Fix It
summary: Shopify QuickBooks integration via Intuit's connector is the quickest route.
body_markdown:
## Connect Shopify to QuickBooks Online step by step


Those three notes feed four stages: check prerequisites, install and authorise the connector, map accounts, then reconcile one test order. Each stage ends with a check you can fail.


### Check Shopify and QuickBooks permissions first


You need a Shopify login that can install apps and a QuickBooks Online login with admin rights. A standard user will fail at the authorisation screen, and the error looks like a connector bug when it's a permissions gap.


Which plan you are on matters too. According to[CFOpresso](https://cfopresso.com/blog/quickbooks-vs-netsuite) , Simple Start runs $19 to $38 a month, so budget for double once the promotion lapses. Essentials is $42.50 to $85, the same doubling between the discounted and list price.


Per[Cfopresso](https://cfopresso.com/blog/quickbooks-vs-netsuite) 's analysis, Plus is $70 to $140. Advanced is $170 to $340, which means Advanced's entry price exceeds Plus's maximum by $30. Price the regular figure, not the promotional one.


Before you pay for any tier, check the connector's listing for which QuickBooks plans it supports.


*Check:* you can open both admin screens and name the plan you are on.


### Stage 2: Install the connector and authorise QuickBooks


Open the Shopify App Store, find the vendor-supported connector, and choose to add the app. When it redirects to QuickBooks, sign in and approve the company file.


If you manage several companies, confirm the name on the consent screen, because connecting the wrong one is the commonest mistake here.


Then set the sync start date. Pick the first day of a fresh accounting period, not today's date. **Orders before that date stay out of QuickBooks** , so an earlier date means backfilling history you may already have booked by hand.


*Check:* the connector shows QuickBooks as connected, with the right company name and your chosen start date.


### Map Shopify accounts, taxes and payouts in QuickBooks


Here, at mapping, is where most sync failures start. Assign each Shopify sales channel to an income account, shipping to its own account, and discounts to a contra-income account.


Map every tax rate to a QuickBooks tax code, because an unmapped rate usually blocks the whole order. Point payment gateway payouts at a clearing account, not your bank account directly.


*Check:* no Shopify line type is left unmapped, and the clearing account is the only account receiving payouts.


Last comes a test sync, stage 4. Place one low-value order with a discount, shipping and tax. Trigger the sync, then open the resulting QuickBooks record and compare it to Shopify line by line.


*Check:* the QuickBooks total, tax and shipping match Shopify to the cent. Only then switch on automatic sync for all orders.
